mainTopic: Things forbidden to use but without מעילה, the measure of the water libation (ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן), and a nest on a הקדש tree
overview: The משנה lists things you may not use, but which carry no מעילה if you do. These are tree roots that cross between private and הקדש land, a spring flowing through a הקדש field, the water in the golden jug for the סוכות water libation, and the ערבה for the מזבח. Once the water is put into the flask, which is a כלי שרת, it does carry מעילה. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק adds that the elders used the ערבה in their לולבים. In the גמרא, ריש לקיש first seems to say that three לוגין in the jug carry מעילה. The גמרא challenges this from the משנה and moves his statement to the flask: there, only three לוגין carry מעילה, while רבי יוחנן says all of it does. The גמרא then asks whether ריש לקיש elsewhere implied that water has no measure, and answers that he was only arguing within מנחם יודאפה's approach. A new משנה then teaches about a nest on a הקדש tree, a nest on an אשירה, and a consecrated forest.

steps.title: Roots that cross between private and consecrated land
steps.stepSummary: Roots of a private tree growing into הקדש land, or roots of a הקדש tree growing into private land: you may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Roots of a privately owned tree that grow into consecrated land, and roots of a consecrated tree that grow into private land: you may not benefit from them, but if you do, there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with its first case of 'forbidden to use, but no מעילה': tree roots that cross the border between private and הקדש land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roots are in a mixed situation, belonging to one owner but growing in the other's ground. Because of this, the רבנן forbid using them from the start. The full מעילה penalty does not apply, because these roots are not plain, fully consecrated property.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה we are learning
An ordinary person, meaning private non-holy property
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
You may not benefit from it at the start, but if you did, there is no מעילה
Using הקדש for yourself; this brings a קרבן and a payment of value plus a fifth

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא נהנין' and 'לא מועלין' are two separate things. The first says you should not use it. The second says that if you did use it, the special מעילה penalty does not apply. Something can be forbidden without carrying מעילה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The roots of a tree belonging to an ordinary person
that come into consecrated land,
and roots of a consecrated tree that come into an ordinary person's land –
one may not benefit from them, and there is no מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׇׁרְשֵׁי אִילָן שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט הַבָּאִין בְּשֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crossing roots are forbidden to use, but carry no מעילה.

steps.title: A spring flowing out of a consecrated field
steps.stepSummary: While a spring is inside a הקדש field, its water may not be used but carries no מעילה. Once it flows out of the field, it may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: A spring that comes out from within a consecrated field: you may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה. Once it has gone outside the field, you may benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. Spring water inside a הקדש field is forbidden to use but carries no מעילה, and once it flows out of the field it is fully permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, unlike the roots, the משנה tells us what removes the restriction: leaving the field. Water that has left the הקדש field is simply ordinary water.

keyTerms.meaning: A spring of flowing water
It went out beyond the field

phrases.english: A spring that comes out
from within the consecrated field –
one may not benefit from it, and there is no מעילה.
Once it has gone outside the field –
one may benefit from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעְיָן שֶׁהוּא יוֹצֵא מִתּוֹךְ הַשָּׂדֶה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spring water inside a הקדש field: forbidden, no מעילה. Outside the field: permitted.

steps.title: Water for the סוכות libation: the jug and the flask
steps.stepSummary: Water in the golden jug may not be used but carries no מעילה. Once it is poured into the flask, it does carry מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The water in the golden jug: you may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה. Once it has been put into the flask, there is מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the water drawn for the סוכות water libation. In the golden jug it is forbidden but carries no מעילה. Once it is placed in the flask, it carries מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The golden jug is not a כלי שרת, so it cannot make the water holy. Still, the water is set aside for the עבודה, so using it is forbidden. The flask is a כלי שרת, so it fully sanctifies the water, and from then on מעילה applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden jug used to draw the water, which is not a כלי שרת
A flask; here the כלי שרת that makes the water holy
A vessel used in the בית המקדש service, which makes what is placed in it holy
The water libation poured on the מזבח on סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's discussion. ריש לקיש will limit the 'no מעילה' rule for the jug.

phrases.english: The water that is in the golden jug –
phrases.notes: This is the water drawn on סוכות to be poured on the מזבח as the water libation.

phrases.english: one may not benefit from it, and there is no מעילה.
Once he put it into the flask –
there is מעילה with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case from the בית המקדש service
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the jug: forbidden, no מעילה. In the flask (a כלי שרת): there is מעילה.

steps.title: The willow for the altar, and the elders' practice
steps.stepSummary: The ערבה for the מזבח is forbidden to use but carries no מעילה. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק reports that the elders used it for their לולבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The willow: you may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: the elders used to benefit from it by using it in their לולבים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last case, the ערבה placed around the מזבח on סוכות. Then רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק tells us about an actual practice of the elders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first opinion, the ערבה is like the earlier cases: forbidden, but no מעילה. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק shows that the elders took from it to fulfill the מצוה of לולב. Using it for a מצוה like this was something the elders permitted themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Willow branches placed around the מזבח on סוכות
They were accustomed; it was their regular practice
The palm branch bundle (with the other species) taken on סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: All four cases in the משנה follow one pattern: forbidden to use, but no מעילה. The jug water is the one case where a change (putting it into the flask) brings full מעילה.

phrases.english: The willow –
one may not benefit from it, and there is no מעילה.
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
The elders were accustomed
to benefit from it in their לולבים.
phrases.notes: He means they took pieces of the מזבח willow to add to their own לולב bundle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case in the list, with an added report of practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערבה is forbidden with no מעילה; the elders used it for their לולבים.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the three לוגין needed for the libation do carry מעילה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש limits the משנה's rule for the jug water. The extra water carries no מעילה, but the three לוגין needed for the libation do.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: ריש לקיש said: There is no מעילה for all of the water, but there is מעילה for three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by having ריש לקיש narrow the משנה's statement about the water in the golden jug.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the jug water has no מעילה. ריש לקיש explains that this applies only to the water beyond what the libation needs. The three לוגין set aside for the libation carry מעילה even while still in the jug.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion explaining the משנה
In all of it, meaning the whole amount in the jug
Three לוג, the amount of water needed for the libation

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש does not disagree with the משנה. He explains which part of the water the משנה's 'no מעילה' covers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement will be the focus of the discussion that follows in the גמרא.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Reish Lakish said:
There is no מעילה for all of it,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the water in the golden jug from the משנה.

phrases.english: but there is מעילה for three לוגין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אֵין מוֹעֲלִין בְּכוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's ruling on the jug water
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra water in the jug has no מעילה; the three לוגין for the libation carry מעילה.

steps.title: The last line of the משנה shows the jug never carries מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says מעילה begins only once the water is in the flask. That implies the jug carries no מעילה at all, even for the three לוגין. This contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the last part of the משנה says that once he put the water into the flask, there is מעילה. That shows that in the first part, while it is still in the jug, there is no מעילה at all, even for three לוגין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's statement from Step 5. It uses the משנה's own wording to do this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the three לוגין in the jug carry מעילה. But the סיפא sets the flask as the point where מעילה begins. That implies nothing in the jug carries מעילה, not even the three needed לוגין.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה
By implication, from this we learn

phrases.english: But the latter clause teaches:
"If he put it into the flask, there is מעילה with them,"
which implies that in the first clause
even with three לוגין there is also no מעילה!
phrases.notes: Three לוגין is the amount needed for the libation, the part ריש לקיש said does carry מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's statement in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the three לוגין in the jug carry מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא sets the flask as the start of מעילה, so the רישא implies the jug has no מעילה at all

steps.title: ריש לקיש's limit was said about the flask
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves ריש לקיש's statement to the סיפא. In the flask, only three לוגין carry מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if ריש לקיש said something, he said it about the last part of the משנה. The משנה says there is מעילה with the water in the flask. On that, ריש לקיש said there is מעילה only with three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says ריש לקיש was actually talking about the flask, not the jug.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jug carries no מעילה at all, just as the משנה implies. ריש לקיש's point is about the flask: only the three לוגין needed for the libation carry מעילה. Extra water there does not.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, meaning the statement belongs somewhere else
A measure of liquid; the libation needs three לוגין

steps.confusionAlert: This replaces Step 5. ריש לקיש is no longer talking about the jug at all. His three-לוגין limit is now about the flask only.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said,
it was said on the latter clause.
"There is מעילה with them":
Reish Lakish said:
there is מעילה only with three לוגין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by moving the statement to the סיפא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the statement to a different clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש was limiting the jug water to three לוגין
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש limits the flask water: only three לוגין carry מעילה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says all the water in the flask carries מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש. Every drop of water in the flask carries מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: there is מעילה with all of the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's opposing view on the water in the flask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש limits מעילה to three לוגין. רבי יוחנן does not set any limit, so even water beyond three לוגין in the flask carries מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: With all of them, here all of the water

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: there is מעילה with all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to ריש לקיש in Step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the water in the flask carries מעילה, not only three לוגין

steps.title: Does ריש לקיש hold that water has a fixed measure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether ריש לקיש's view means water has a fixed measure. It starts a challenge from a משנה: one who pours the סוכות water outside the מקדש on סוכות is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that ריש לקיש holds water has a fixed measure? But we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר said, one who pours the festival water as a libation, on the festival, outside the מקדש, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions ריש לקיש's view and brings a משנה to challenge it. This step is setting up the challenge, which continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Limiting מעילה to three לוגין means water has a set amount, like wine. The גמרא brings a משנה about the water libation to test that idea. The source for that משנה is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed measure or amount
The water for the libation on סוכות
Outside the מקדש courtyard
Liable, here for offering outside the מקדש

phrases.english: Is this to say that Reish Lakish holds:
water has a fixed measure?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
Rabbi Eliezer said:
phrases.notes: In the next line the name appears as רבי אלעזר; the text varies here, but both refer to the author of this משנה.

phrases.english: One who pours the festival water as a libation,
on the festival, outside, is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְקָסָבַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ יֵשׁ שִׁיעוּר לַמַּיִם וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind ריש לקיש's view in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that only three לוגין of water carry מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His view implies water has a fixed measure; a משנה about the water libation is brought to test this

steps.title: The source: water libation and wine libation are learned together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא learns from the word נסכיהם that there are two libations, water and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said in the name of מנחם יודאפה: רבי אלעזר said this following רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא learns from the word "their libations" that one is the water libation and one is the wine libation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source of the משנה it just quoted. This builds the challenge further; the conclusion comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for pouring the water outside comes from רבי עקיבא's reading. The plural word נסכיהם covers both the water libation and the wine libation. This places water in the same verse as wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Following the view of
Their libations; the plural hints at two libations
The water libation poured on סוכות
The wine libation

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם מְנַחֵם יוֹדָאפָה:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Menachem Yodafa:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אָמַר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said this following the view of Rabbi Akiva,
who expounds "their libations":

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד נִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם, וְאֶחָד נִיסּוּךְ הַיַּיִן.
phrases.english: one is the water libation, and one is the wine libation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם מְנַחֵם יוֹדָאפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה quoted in Step 9, building the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that water has a fixed measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source connects the water libation to the wine libation through the word נסכיהם; the conclusion comes in the next part of the גמרא

steps.title: ריש לקיש: If water is like wine, it should need three לוגין
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן. If water is learned from wine, water should also have wine's measure of three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: If so, then just as wine is three לוגין, water should also be three לוגין!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back on רבי יוחנן's explanation from the last step. If water and wine come from the same word, they should share the same measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, רבי עקיבא learned from the word נסכיהם that there are two libations, water and wine. ריש לקיש argues that if they are linked this closely, water should copy wine's measure of three לוגין. His exclamation suggests he finds that result hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: Plural of לוֹג, a liquid measure
If just as... so too... (a way of comparing two cases)
Wine (here, the wine libation)

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
If so, just as wine is three log,
so too water should be three log!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה יַיִן שָׁלֹשׁ לוּגִּין, אַף מַיִם שָׁלֹשׁ לוּגִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's explanation that רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא's reading of נסכיהם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the water libation is learned from the wine libation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If water comes from the same source as wine, water should also take wine's three-לוג measure.

steps.title: Inference: ריש לקיש must hold water has no measure
steps.stepSummary: From ריש לקיש's challenge, the גמרא infers that he holds water has no fixed measure. That clashes with his earlier view about three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that ריש לקיש holds there is no measure for the water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from ריש לקיש's words and uses it as a challenge. His question only works if he thinks water really has no set measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ריש לקיש thought water needs three לוגין, his question would not be a problem at all. So it seems he holds water has no measure. But earlier, ריש לקיש said three לוגין of water carry מעילה. That only makes sense if water does have a measure, so his views seem to contradict each other. This completes the challenge the גמרא opened in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; we can learn from this
There is no fixed measure

phrases.english: By inference, Reish Lakish holds
there is no measure for the water!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּסָבַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אֵין שִׁיעוּר לַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from step 11 and turns it into a challenge against ריש לקיש's earlier ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that three לוגין of water in the flask carry מעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His challenge only makes sense if water has no measure, but his ruling about three לוגין assumes water has a measure.

steps.title: He was speaking within מנחם יודאפה's approach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש asked his question according to מנחם יודאפה's reasoning, not according to his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to the reasoning of מנחם יודאפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. ריש לקיש was arguing within someone else's approach, so his question does not show his own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's challenge was aimed at the approach of מנחם יודאפה, which רבי יוחנן had cited. It tested that approach on its own terms. So ריש לקיש can still hold that water has a measure, and his three-לוג ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the reasoning of...
He is saying (he said it)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's question about three לוגין was asked within מנחם יודאפה's approach. It does not show his own view, so his earlier ruling stands.

phrases.english: He said it according to the reasoning of Menachem Yodafa.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the statement to another view: the question was asked according to someone else's approach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's question shows that he holds water has no measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only argued according to מנחם יודאפה's approach. In his own view, water does have a measure, so his three-לוג ruling for the flask stands.

steps.title: New משנה: A nest on a הקדש tree, a nest on an אשירה, and a consecrated forest
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches three rules. A nest on top of a הקדש tree is forbidden to benefit from, but there is no מעילה. A nest on an אשירה is knocked down with a pole. If someone consecrates a forest, everything in it carries מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A nest on top of a הקדש tree: one may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה for it. A nest on an אשירה: one should knock it down with a pole. One who consecrates a forest: there is מעילה for all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: things connected to a consecrated tree or forest. It gives three short rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a nest on a הקדש tree, the משנה separates two things that usually go together. Benefit is forbidden, but there is still no מעילה. For a nest on an אשירה, the משנה tells you how to get it: knock it down with a pole. When a whole forest is consecrated, מעילה applies to everything in it.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird's nest
A tree that is worshipped as עבודה זרה
He should knock it down with a pole
A forest or grove of trees

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that 'forbidden to benefit' always means 'there is מעילה'. In the first case, benefit is forbidden, yet there is no מעילה.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַקֵּן שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ –
phrases.english: MISHNA: A nest that is on top of a consecrated tree –
one may not benefit from it, but there is no misuse liability.
One on a tree worshipped as idolatry – he should knock it down with a pole.
One who consecrates a forest –
there is misuse liability for all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the water-libation discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nest on a הקדש tree is forbidden to benefit from but carries no מעילה. A nest on an אשירה is knocked down with a pole. In a consecrated forest, everything carries מעילה.
